department: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

deadline.value: International applicants apply by February 1 for fall, which is also the departmental fellowship deadline.
deadline.quote: Fall Applications Domestic (US Citizen or Permanent Resident): May 1 International (Everyone else, no matter the visa type or where you are going to school): February 1 | To be considered for Electrical and Computer Engineering departmental fellowships, please submit your CAS application by no later than February 1.

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for this field; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Admission is through the department, but you are advised to contact faculty in your area about research assistantships.
supervisor.quote: The students are advised to contact the faculty in their areas of interest for consideration for research assistantships.

funding.value: Up to 50 fellowships/TAships ($2,500 a month plus tuition and fees) for incoming PhD students; other support comes from faculty RAs.
funding.quote: The department offers up to 50 Fellowships and Teaching Assistantships that cover tuition and fees, as well as a $2,500 monthly stipend, for incoming Ph.D. students.

entry_route.value: The pages checked do not say whether a master's is needed.

app_fee.value: International applicants pay $90 to Texas A&M plus $58 to EngineeringCAS.
app_fee.quote: Texas A&M application fee ($65 for domestic students, $90 for international) | Engineering CAS application fee ($58)

gre_general.value: GRE is optional; strong scores can help applicants with a lower GPA.
gre_general.quote: The GRE is optional for all applicants.

notes: Computer Engineering PhD is offered by both ECE and CSE. Separate funding offers may follow admission.
